Four months in. Could you actually prove it is working?

You logged the doses. You did the sessions. You hit the protein. And if someone asked you tomorrow whether any of it was working, the honest answer would still be a shrug — because the evidence is sitting in three apps that have never heard of each other.

My Body is three apps too. The difference is one account, so they share a timeline and the answer is just there.

Free on the App Store.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

The reason you stopped logging last time was the logging.

Last session's numbers are already filled in, the rest timer starts itself, and the plate maths is done. Three seconds a set — because every extra tap is a rep you did not do.

Free on the App Store.

posts.caption:
This is the sentence you want to be able to say out loud.

"Down six kilos. Strength held. Protein at 142 a day."

That takes three datasets, and almost nobody has them in one place — so most people can prove the first part and guess at the rest. My Body is three apps on one account, which is the only reason the sentence writes itself.

My Body Pro unlocks all three, £49.99 a year with the first week free. The core of every app stays free.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

You will not remember what you did in March.

You think you will. Nobody does. Six months from now the doses, the sessions and the weeks you actually held the line will have blurred into a general sense that you were trying quite hard.

That is the whole job: something quietly writing it down, so the effort still exists later.

Free to start. Three apps, one account.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

The reason you gave up tracking last time was the setting up.

Point your camera at the label. On-device text recognition reads it and builds the protocol — no upload, and the image never leaves your phone. That is the setup, done.

Free: one protocol, logging, reminders, site rotation.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

I needed to know whether any of it was actually doing anything.

So the strength chart marks the day you started. Move takes that date from Optimise, because they share an account — a standalone workout app has no idea what you are running, so it can never draw that line.

The overlay is in Pro, which covers all three apps for £49.99 a year, first week free.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

I never turned this on. It just knew.

Fuel saw a GLP-1 protocol logged in Optimise and switched itself to muscle-retention mode — protein first, calories second, portions sized for an appetite that is not there.

There is no setting for it. That is the point of one account.

The weight is coming off. That is not the part to watch.

On a GLP-1 you are almost certainly already eating under, so counting down from a number you will undershoot anyway tells you very little. What decides how much of the loss is fat and how much is muscle is protein.

Fuel leads with grams-to-go and puts calories second. Free to use.

Not medical advice. Talk to your prescriber.

Week one of charging money. Here's the number I'd rather not post.

[subscribers] subscribers, [downloads] downloads, [refunds] refunds, [cancellations] cancellations.

Building this in the open, which means the bad weeks get posted at the same size as the good ones.

You are doing everything right. You just cannot see it yet.

Your strength says one thing, your protein says another, and your weight says a third — and none of them, alone, answers the question you are actually asking.

The alignment score is one number for how well all three line up with the goal you set. A single-app tracker cannot draw it, because it does not have the data.

In My Body Pro. First week free.

Nobody in my life knows I am on this.

That is more common than anyone admits, and it is why this app is built the way it is. It works with the phone in airplane mode. Progress photos never leave the device. Face ID on the app. No ads, no data sales, no tracking, no analytics on your health data.

When a health app is free and you cannot see how it makes money, you already know how it makes money. Ours is the subscription, on purpose.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

"I only want the workout one."

Completely fair, and it is how most people arrive. Every app has a plan of its own, and it upgrades into the full family whenever you want the other two — without paying twice.

The bundle exists because it is cheaper than three, not because you are obliged to take it.

You already have the answer. It is sitting in three different places.

A fortnight of protocol. The same fortnight of training. The same fortnight of food. Separately, each one is a chart you glance at. Together, on one x-axis, they are the only honest picture of what you have been doing.

One account means one timeline. Every insight in the product comes from that and nothing else.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

I did not want to charge you three times for one body.

Three apps, one account, built to share data from the first day. Charging separately for each of them would have been taking money for a problem we deliberately did not create.

So My Body Pro is one subscription across all three — £49.99 a year, first week free, and the core of every app stays free.

Roughly two apps' worth of money for three apps. That was the target when we set it.

A doctor asked what I had actually been doing. I could not answer.

Everything was written down somewhere. None of it was written down together, so there was no version of the last six months I could show anyone — including myself.

That is the app. Free to start, three apps, one account.

18+. Personal tracking, not medical advice.

You were worried I would take something away.

I would not. Every feature that was free on launch day is still free and stays free. My Body Pro added the deeper end on top — full history, the analytics, unlimited protocols, the cross-app picture.

One subscription, three apps, £49.99 a year, first week free. Link in bio.
